chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Ibrahim ibn Maymoun who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man whose clothes fall upon the body of the deceased. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it had been washed, then do not wash what hit your clothes from it; and if it had not been washed, then wash what hit your clothes from it — meaning when the dead body is cold.'
ai.seo_question: Do I need to wash my clothes if they touch a dead body?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the impurity (najāsah) of a deceased body is contingent upon the cooling of the body after death; thus, if the body has not yet cooled, any fluid or residue transferring to clothing is considered impure and requires washing. However, if the body has already undergone ritual washing (ghusl) and cooled, the residue is deemed pure, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the state of the body at the time of contact determines the ruling. This distinction highlights the nuanced approach to taharah in al-Kafi, linking physical states to legal purity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Ibrahim Bin Maymoun who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man whose clothes fall upon a body of the deceased. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it (dead body) had been washed, so you would not wash whatever hits your clothes from it; and if it was so that it had not been washed, so wash whatever hits your clothes from it – meaning when the dead body is cold’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Ibrahim ibn al-Maymun who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man whose clothes fall on a dead body. He (the Imam) said, ‘If the dead body is given Ghusl (bath), then it is not necessary to wash such clothes, but if it is not given Ghusl (bath) yet, one must wash such clothes - and that is, when the dead body has become cold.’”
